name: New Orleans
tagline: 25-cent martinis at a 19th-century classic, and beignets worth the line every time.

Commander's Palace.description: Creole and Cajun cuisine since the 19th century, winner of seven James Beard awards. The 25-cent martini lunch is a local ritual.

Café du Monde.description: Beignets and chicory coffee at the French Market since the 19th century, with a constant line and zero pretension.

Galatoire's.description: French Creole cuisine on Bourbon Street since 1905, now run by the fourth generation of the Galatoire family.

Dooky Chase's Restaurant.description: Creole cooking since 1941 and a historic meeting point of the Civil Rights Movement, with Martin Luther King Jr. among its visitors.

Casamento's.description: New Orleans' most famous oyster loaf since 1919, in a spot tiled floor to ceiling in century-old Italian tile.
